                    ### Question
                    A 55-year-old Caucasian male presents for a routine colonoscopy. A polyp is found in the patient's transverse colon and is found to be cancerous on histological evaluation. Upon examination, it is found that these cancerous cells have decreased MHC class I expression on their surface. Which immune system cell is most capable of killing these tumor cells?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Natural killer cells
opb. B-cells
opc. Macrophages
opd. Eosinophils
ope. Cytotoxic T-cells

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
Cancerous cells with decreased MHC class I expression are less recognizable by cytotoxic T-cells, which rely on MHC class I for antigen presentation. This reduction in recognition leads to an increased susceptibility of these tumor cells to natural killer (NK) cells, which can detect and kill cells that exhibit stress signals or abnormal MHC expression. The consensus in immunology supports that NK cells are particularly effective against tumor cells that evade detection by the adaptive immune response due to low MHC class I expression. Therefore, the most capable immune system cell for killing these tumor cells is the natural killer cell.
